newsitem.title: FRANCE: BRUSSELS MUSSELS CHAIN STOCK SELLS LIKE HOT CAKES.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS MUSSELS CHAIN STOCK SELLS LIKE HOT CAKES.

text.p: The listing in Paris of Belgian restaurant chain Leon de Bruxelles was delayed on Tuesday until May 5 after the shares were more than 130 times oversubscribed.
The SBF French Bourses' Association said that while 212,500 shares at 140 francs ($24) had been offered on the Second Marche secondary market, there was a demand for 27,779,507 shares.
On May 5, 244,375 shares will be offered at 175 francs.

Leon de Bruxelles, which started out in Belgium but now also has restaurants in Paris, specialises in the Belgian traditional dish of "moules-frites" -- mussels and fries -- served in many varieties and tastes and usually accompanied by a glass of beer.
The original offer had valued the restaurant group at 300 million francs, at 22 times its expected 1997 profits.
With the new price it is valued at 375 million francs, or 27.7 times 1997 earnings.
Leon de Bruxelles closed 1996 with profit of 9.7 million francs on sales of 126.3 million. It expects 1997 profit of 13.5 million francs on turnover of 155 million.
The company was started in 1893 and opened its first restaurant in Paris in 1989 where it proved an interesting mix between traditional tastes and fast food.

Its notoriety was helped by a heavy and bright advertisment campaign with big posters in the Paris metro with slogans as "You do not have to go all the way to Brussels for mussels-fries" and "At Leon de Bruxelles it is polite to eat with your fingers and ask for gifts."

The initial public offering (IPO) of Leon de Bruxelles SA is managed by Caisse Centrale des Banques Populaires, Banque d'Orsay and brokers Jean-Pierre Pinaton and Europe Finance et Industrie. ($ = 5.832 French Francs)
